plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Trim broad index holdings (SPY, QQQ) to reduce concentration.
Reduce exposure to individual tech names (CRWD, SMH) that are weak.
Add to income-generating ETF (QQQI) for stability.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation with reduced leverage.
Expect lower volatility and a more defensive posture.
conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for lower, steadier returns with reduced risk. Expect around 1.5% per month, with significantly lower potential drawdowns. Capital preservation is the primary goal.

plan: Slightly trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to maintain minimal exposure.
Reduce concentration in broad index ETFs (SPY, QQQ).
Exit the weak semiconductor holding (SMH).
Trim the income ETF (QQQI) slightly.
Initiate a new position in a top-rated scanner setup (SNOW).
This plan balances risk reduction with selective growth opportunities.
balanced.read: This balanced approach seeks risk-first growth, targeting around 2.5% per month. It reduces concentration and leverage while adding a promising new name. Drawdowns are expected to be moderate.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) as per aggressive mandate.
Trim broad index ETFs (SPY, QQQ) to fund growth areas.
Exit the weak semiconductor holding (SMH) and income ETF (QQQI).
Initiate a new position in a top-rated scanner setup (SNOW).
This plan aggressively pursues growth by leaning into leverage and strong setups.
Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger potential drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan targets around 4% per month by increasing leverage and concentrating on high-scoring setups. Be aware that leveraged ETFs decay and this strategy carries substantially higher risk and potential for large, rapid losses. Strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and volatile tech/semis (QQQ, CRWD, SMH).
Trim broad index (SPY) to reallocate capital.
Significantly increase allocation to income ETF (QQQI).
This plan prioritizes generating steady monthly income.
Focus is on capital preservation and reliable distributions.
Expect lower growth potential but also very low drawdowns.
income.read: This income-focused plan aims for approximately 1% per month through distributions, prioritizing stability and cash flow. It minimizes leverage and volatile assets. While distributions are not guaranteed and NAV can fall, the goal is consistent income generation with low drawdowns.
